text:
ken-support: FYI customer reports daily usage CSV and dashboard disagree around day cutoff for their org in Pacific/Apia (UTC+14). CSV shows last 14 hours lumped into previous day.

acme-cs: repro + sample attached — export for 2026-07-05 (account 98123) shows totals for '2026-07-04' that include events with timestamps after 00:00 local. here's a tiny excerpt:```date,client_id,tokens
2026-07-04,98123,12456
2026-07-05,98123,0
```we expect the 12456 to be on 2026-07-05 (local).

maya: thanks — can you paste exact repro steps (how you generated CSV) and whether this is also visible in the UI charts?

ken-support: steps from customer: 1) Console > Billing > Usage export > choose "daily" > timezone set to "Org timezone (Pacific/Apia)" 2) export CSV 3) compare with Console daily chart (set to org timezone). They say chart and CSV disagree — chart shows zero on 7/5 until ~00:30 then spike, CSV has the previous day carrying the tokens.

liz-eng-runtime: tagging in runtime team. quick question: are the aggregator and export pipeline both reading the same timezone field? if not, this can cause a day-split for tz east of UTC. can you share account id and an example event ts?

ken-support: account 98123. example event iso: `2026-07-05T00:10:22+14:00`. customer says exports are still showing it under 2026-07-04.

liz-eng-runtime: running a quick check on the aggregator logic — the daily rollup job uses `date_trunc('day', at_time_zone(event_ts, 'UTC'))` in one place but exports use `at_time_zone(event_ts, org_tz)` when bucketing. that mismatch would shift day boundaries for +TZ orgs.

deploy-bot: deploy successful: export-pipeline@v2.3.7 -> rolled 2026-07-04T02:12Z (commit d9f4b2e).

oliver-sre: that deploy touched the export serialization path last week. probable candidate: a change that set `use_utc=true` only for UI queries but left CSV export reading `org_tz`. mitigations: 1) hotfix export to respect `use_utc` flag, 2) force both chart & CSV to use UTC for pivot until we align.

liz-eng-runtime: agreed. plan: patch export translation to use unified tz helper from runtime lib (patch queued), add regression test for +12/+14 offsets, and backfill small window for affected accounts. ETA ~4h for hotfix rollout, then 6-12h for backfill job.

ken-support: pinging customer with interim guidance: ask them to set export timezone to UTC (if they can) as temporary workaround. will update when hotfix is live. :thumbsup:

acme-cs: appreciated — we rely on daily exports for billing reconciliation, please escalate if needed.

liz-eng-runtime: escalating to infra if backfill needs more IO. I'll post PR link and rollout notes here once ready.

ken-support: thanks all, will mark high priority and keep thread open.
